items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: And when the Clarence asked me, do some recording? I said yeah, do some recording.

ctx.x: I'll have to look for it and see if I can find it. It's made around 1931 or 1932.

Very good record. Well that's a fairly late one though. Yeah. Eight piece banner. Eight piece banner. I can't even take the name of it. I'm going to look at the house when I go home. I might have it. I don't have it but there's one outside and I can't hear nothing in front of it. If I can find it I'll call you and give you the name. I'm going to look one day. Well they might have it in one of those books. Yeah. I don't remember seeing it in the jazz record I look for. I like that record very much. Was Floyd Casey…
Would Clarence be there when the records were made?

items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: Stratford came out there and wanted a group to go on the boat in the daytime around the St. Louis day ride. We had a plan of presence I was working with. And we all got six pieces we played in the day boat every day.

ctx.x: Did you ever get outside St. Louis in those years to play? Did you get jobs on the road?

No, not until I left St. Louis. During those years, before I left St. Louis, I would do some work. I married young, so I had to work. I didn't labor and work, packing house. I did work in the foundry. I played a lot in the nightclubs, two and three nights a week out on the outskirts. But after I left St. Louis in 1920 I went out on the coast, Seattle. And I've been playing music ever since. I went out that state about two years, played on the nightclub. A fellow came to St. Louis and wanted some musicians. I went…

items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: Clarence got recorded, he was calling him Cuzz. Cuzz, what you got up? Can you go on some of your recording dates that they come up? ... He said, yeah, come on now, Cuzz. Come on, I got a date, so, so, so.

ctx.x: Well he was about anything class way man, King Oliver had something in there to do, he'd come to record it. Whenever he come in time, he'd make some recordings with his band. And most of the time King Oliver made his own band so he didn't have to have nobody. When Clarence was going to make something from his group, he'd set King in and all that. Always make some money see. Well Williams didn't have a regular group working anyway. No, I don't remember having a group in any spot at all. But most of the time he…

That's a good record. With whose band were you working at the time you made most of your recordings for Clarence Williams? Once I was working with Alain Rolf and Leroy Tiff, the band saved by Connie Zinn.
